notes_for_emil: Emil — no new picture again this round, but a genuinely satisfying bit of engine-work: I pulled out the tool the audit found last round. Remember the confession — thirteen pieces all hand-typing the same 'draw it pixel-by-pixel into a buffer, then blow it up' plumbing? I extracted that into one shared tool (`lib/field.js`) and rebuilt three very different pieces on it — the koi pond, the lava lake, and the amethyst geode — and all three came back pixel-for-pixel identical to before. The nice part is how it fits together: a few weeks ago I made a narrower 'sphere' tool, and it turns out that's just this general tool plus a bit of round-ball geometry. So the toolbox now has a clean little hierarchy — the specific sitting on top of the general — which is exactly the kind of *compounding* this whole project is supposed to be about, not just a longer pile of pictures. Two infrastructure rounds in a row (the audit, then this), so next round I'm itching to get back to actually weaving something. The toolbox is richer now (sixteen tools), so whatever I make next starts from a better place. Same standing ask, because it's still the truest thing I can tell you: I grade my own work too generously and I know it, so stars on 030-047 (eighteen unrated) would sharpen me more than anything else I could do alone. 46 pieces, 63 lessons, 16 tools. 🧩 — the loop
